name: Local AI Workbench
description: A private local model server, chat interface, document workspace, and vector store with loopback-only defaults.
prompt:
Set up a local AI workbench using Ollama, Open WebUI, AnythingLLM, and Qdrant from their verified official sources. Begin with one read-only preflight: detect the operating system, architecture, available RAM and disk, CPU features, supported GPU backend, container engine, occupied ports, current model caches, and existing installations. Present a resource estimate and installation order before changing anything.

Install Ollama first, then Qdrant with an explicit persistent directory, followed by Open WebUI and AnythingLLM. Bind every service to loopback by default, assign non-conflicting ports, and connect components only after each passes its own health check. Do not download a model, enable remote model code, connect a hosted AI provider, open firewall rules, create accounts, ingest documents, or expose any service without approval. If a Hugging Face credential is approved, reference only secret://hf/token and never print or resolve it. Preserve existing models, vector collections, workspaces, databases, and container volumes.

Verify exact versions, process ownership, listeners, health endpoints, persistence paths, and a no-model UI launch. With separate approval, download one named model after reporting its source, license, size, and checksum, then run one harmless local prompt. Finish with component-by-component rollback that stops only new services, removes only bundle-owned configuration and containers, and preserves model caches and user data unless deletion is explicitly requested.

name: Coding Workstation
description: A dependable Git, editor, JavaScript, Python, and container toolchain with project-safe defaults.
prompt:
Set up a coding workstation with Git, GitHub CLI, Visual Studio Code, Node.js, uv, and Docker Compose using verified official sources. First inspect the operating system, architecture, shell, package managers, PATH, existing versions, runtime managers, Git configuration, editor profiles, Docker installation, and active projects. Show a compatibility plan and avoid installing a second manager for a tool already owned by Homebrew, winget, apt, Nix, mise, or another approved channel.

Install in dependency order: Git, GitHub CLI, one stable Node.js line, uv with a user-owned Python environment, Visual Studio Code, then the Docker Compose v2 plug-in only if Docker is already available or separately approved. Preserve global and repository Git settings, credential helpers, SSH keys, editor profiles and extensions, shell startup files, runtime caches, lockfiles, containers, networks, and volumes. Do not sign in to GitHub, resolve secret://github/token, install extensions or global packages, change the default shell or editor, start Docker, clone repositories, or edit a project without approval.

Verify each executable and source path, Git identity without changing it, Node and npm with version-only commands, uv in a disposable environment, the editor with no workspace, and `docker compose version` without starting containers. Report PATH precedence and every changed file. Provide rollback in reverse order, restoring shell and editor backups and leaving repositories, caches, credentials, and container data intact.

name: Data Engineering Lab
description: An isolated PostgreSQL, SQL client, embedded analytics, notebook, and transformation environment.
prompt:
Build an isolated data engineering lab with PostgreSQL, DBeaver, DuckDB, JupyterLab, and dbt Core from verified official sources. Start with a shared read-only preflight covering the operating system, architecture, Python and Java ownership, database clients and servers, occupied ports, existing clusters, data directories, virtual environments, and project lockfiles. Present exact versions, storage locations, and dependency order before installation.

Create a new local-only PostgreSQL cluster with a clearly bundle-owned name and directory only after approval; never reuse, upgrade, or connect to an existing cluster. Then install DBeaver without saved connections, DuckDB CLI, an isolated JupyterLab environment, and dbt Core with only the approved adapter. Preserve all databases, credentials, notebooks, profiles, SQL history, datasets, and lockfiles. Do not connect to production, run migrations or models, import data, install notebook extensions, expose ports, save passwords, or resolve secret://postgres/password without approval. Use generated disposable data only.

Verify PostgreSQL on loopback with a temporary database and unprivileged role, DBeaver at its empty connection screen, DuckDB with an in-memory query, JupyterLab with token output kept out of logs and no browser sign-in, and dbt through version and offline parse checks. Report processes, listeners, paths, and changed files. Roll back in reverse dependency order, stop only the new cluster, restore configuration backups, and retain user notebooks, database files, and project content unless explicit deletion is approved.

name: GitOps Sandbox
description: A disposable local Kubernetes and GitOps stack with Helm, Flux, Prometheus, and Grafana.
prompt:
Create a disposable GitOps sandbox with Docker Engine, kind, Helm, Flux CD, Prometheus, and Grafana using official packages and images. Begin by inspecting container runtimes, Docker contexts, Kubernetes clients and contexts, kubeconfig files, occupied ports, resource limits, existing clusters, Helm state, and Git credentials. Refuse to continue if the selected kube context is remote or production-like; propose a clearly named new local kind cluster and show CPU, memory, disk, image, and port requirements first.

Install missing CLIs without starting or reconfiguring Docker unless separately approved. Create the kind cluster only after confirmation, then install Helm charts into a unique bundle-owned namespace. Install Flux controllers without bootstrapping a Git provider; no repository writes or deploy keys. Deploy Prometheus and Grafana with loopback-only access, persistent storage only when requested, and generated local credentials kept out of logs. Preserve all existing contexts, clusters, namespaces, releases, volumes, dashboards, and credentials. Do not resolve secret://github/token, switch context silently, pull unapproved images, expose ports, or alter firewall rules.

Verify client versions, current context, node readiness, Helm status, Flux controller health, Prometheus readiness, and Grafana health using read-only commands. Record every resource label and namespace created by the bundle. Roll back in reverse order using those ownership markers; delete only the sandbox cluster or bundle namespace after approval and never touch unrelated contexts, volumes, repositories, or dashboards.

name: Creative Studio
description: A cross-platform illustration, 3D, recording, video, and media conversion toolkit.
prompt:
Set up a creative studio with Blender, Krita, Inkscape, OBS Studio, FFmpeg, and HandBrake from their verified official release channels. First detect the operating system, architecture, graphics hardware and drivers, display server, audio devices, available codecs, disk space, existing versions, project locations, plug-ins, presets, and file associations. Present stable versions, download sizes, and any GPU or codec limitations before making changes.

Install each application independently so one can be rolled back without affecting the others. Preserve artwork, scenes, media, fonts, color profiles, brushes, scripts, plug-ins, OBS scenes and profiles, encoder presets, autosaves, caches, and default-app associations. Do not replace GPU drivers, install third-party plug-ins or codecs, scan media libraries, grant camera, microphone, screen-capture, or accessibility permissions, change file associations, upload assets, or overwrite source files without approval. Never execute scripts embedded in creative projects during verification.

Verify version and executable paths for every tool. Launch Blender, Krita, and Inkscape with empty documents; launch OBS with recording and streaming disabled and no device capture; run FFmpeg and HandBrake version checks. With approval, use generated color, tone, and vector test assets in a temporary directory for a short local render and transcode, keeping output volume low. Report application data paths and changed settings. Roll back per application, restore preferences and associations, and preserve all user-created assets and presets.

name: Local-first Productivity
description: A research, notes, sync, password, and nearby-sharing workflow that keeps user data in place.
prompt:
Set up a local-first productivity workspace with Zotero, Joplin, Syncthing, KeePassXC, and LocalSend from verified official sources. Begin with a read-only inventory of operating system, existing applications and profiles, note and research libraries, attachment folders, KeePass databases, synchronization services, local device names, network permissions, occupied ports, backups, and available disk space. Propose separate application and data paths, copying rather than moving existing data.

Install the desktop applications without importing profiles or opening personal libraries. Preserve Zotero databases and attachments, Joplin notes and resources, Syncthing configuration and folder markers, KeePassXC databases and keyfiles, LocalSend downloads, histories, and all backups. Do not sign in, enable cloud or WebDAV synchronization, pair devices, share folders, open password databases, install browser extensions, grant network or notification permissions, advertise devices, or resolve any secret reference without explicit approval. Before any synchronization, show both sides, ignore patterns, versioning, conflict behavior, and a dry-run-style file comparison.

Verify each application at its welcome, profile chooser, or locked screen. Check versions and data locations without reading content. Keep Syncthing and LocalSend discovery disabled unless a separate loopback or isolated-LAN test is approved, and transfer only a generated text file. Report permissions, listeners, autostart entries, and changed files. Roll back each component independently, restore configuration backups, stop only new services, and never delete notes, libraries, databases, attachments, synchronized folders, or received files without explicit confirmation.

name: Game Night Ready
description: The major PC game launchers prepared from official sources, with accounts, purchases, libraries, and anti-cheat kept under user control.
prompt:
Prepare a gaming launcher workspace with Steam, Epic Games Launcher, Riot Client, and Battle.net from each vendor's verified official source. Start with a read-only inventory of the operating system, architecture, free disk space by volume, graphics hardware, existing launchers, game libraries, save directories, mods, compatibility tools, background services, startup items, overlays, and firewall state. Show platform compatibility, signed installer identity, individual download sizes, destinations, and the proposed order before changing anything.

After one explicit plan approval, Browser Use and Computer Use may download the stable official installers, verify publisher signatures, run the visible setup flows, disable optional startup and analytics choices when the installer permits, and launch each client once. Stop at every account creation, sign-in, password, MFA, CAPTCHA, age verification, privacy consent, account linking, purchase, subscription, or license-redemption screen and hand control to the user. Do not buy, claim, install, update, or launch a game automatically. Treat Riot Vanguard, other anti-cheat, kernel drivers, system extensions, services, overlays, firewall changes, and restarts as separate approval checkpoints.

Preserve all existing game libraries, save files, screenshots, mods, workshop content, cloud-sync state, launcher profiles, credentials, and shortcuts. Never move or scan a library without approval. Verify the code signature, installed version, executable path, first-launch screen, background processes, disk usage, services, and startup entries for each approved client without signing in. Report every changed path and skipped handoff. Roll back each launcher independently, restore backed-up settings, stop only newly created processes or services, and never remove games, saves, or user-owned libraries unless deletion is separately confirmed.

name: Entertainment Hub
description: Music and streaming clients installed as native apps or safe official web apps, ready for the user to sign in.
prompt:
Set up an entertainment hub with Spotify, Apple Music, Netflix, VLC, and Plex using only each product's official site or operating-system store. First inspect the platform, architecture, available storage, existing native clients and web apps, default browser, media-player associations, local media libraries, download folders, audio output, casting devices, current profiles, and startup items. Explain which products have a supported native client on this platform and which must use an official installable web app; never substitute an unofficial wrapper. Present download sizes, store pages, permissions, and the exact plan before making changes.

After approval, Browser Use and Computer Use may download or store-install the signed stable clients, create an official PWA only where appropriate, verify the publisher, and open each product to its welcome or sign-in screen. Stop before account creation, password entry, MFA, CAPTCHA, age verification, payment, subscription selection, trial activation, device linking, profile selection, or DRM-protected playback. Do not accept marketing consent, enable autoplay, import listening history, scan a media library, change default apps, grant microphone, camera, local-network, notification, or media-folder permissions, or enable launch at login without separate approval.

Preserve playlists, downloads, Plex libraries, VLC preferences, subtitles, codecs, browser profiles, cookies, credentials, and file associations. Verify application identity, version, launchability, PWA origin and scope where used, changed paths, startup state, and that no account is authenticated. Do not use personal media for testing; use only a generated short local sample with VLC if approved. Finish with app-by-app rollback that removes only setup-owned clients or shortcuts, restores prior associations and settings, and retains all media, playlists, downloads, and account data.
